name: Syntactic Complexity
description: Measures the structural depth and grammatical intricacy of sentences by analyzing parse trees and dependency distances. While Large Language Models can generate perfectly grammatical text, they tend to optimize for predictive safety, resulting in a 'syntactic flatness'. This means their sentences often share a similar level of grammatical complexity, avoiding both overly simple fragments and highly tangled, deeply nested human-like structures. Humans naturally vary their syntactic complexity—mixing sharp, simple clauses with deep, complex subordinations to create narrative rhythm.
mechanism: The algorithm parses sentences into constituency and dependency trees to calculate multiple complexity indices: mean parse tree depth, maximum dependency distance, subordination ratio, and T-unit length. It then evaluates the variance of these indices across the entire text. If a text maintains a highly homogenous, moderate-to-high level of syntactic complexity without the natural 'ebbs and flows' characteristic of human cognitive processing, it is flagged as procedurally generated.
useCase: Highly effective for advanced academic papers, long-form journalism, and creative writing, where true syntactic diversity is a hallmark of human stylistic mastery.
strengths:
• Captures deep grammatical fingerprints that are incredibly difficult for humans to manually prompt an AI to fake.
• Highly resilient to deliberate vocabulary replacement (paraphrasing), as the underlying structural 'skeleton' of the sentences remains undisturbed.
limitations:
• Computationally expensive; requires parsing full syntactic trees for every sentence.
• May flag highly regimented human writing, such as technical manuals or specific legal documents, where syntactic uniformity is a required convention.
parameters:
Analysis: Constituency & Dependency Parsing
Metric: Mean Tree Depth, Dependency Distance, & Complexity Variance
Output: 0-100 Syntactic Flatness (Algorithmic Homogeneity) Score
accuracy: High — 80-86% accuracy on long-form texts. One of the most robust structural indicators available when analyzing sufficient word counts (500+ words).

references.title: Lu, X. (2010). Automatic Analysis of Syntactic Complexity in Second Language Writing. International Journal of Corpus Linguistics.
Herbold, S. et al. (2023). A Large-Scale Comparison of Human-Written Versus ChatGPT-Generated Essays. Scientific Reports.
